text.p: Adidas AG, the German sportswear maker, said Tuesday that its profits jumped by 33 percent jump in first quarter on strong sales of training shoes and sports clothing.

The company, known for its three-striped logo, said net profits rose to 169 million marks ($97.9 million) from 127 million marks ($73.5 million) as earnings per share surged to 3.72 marks ($2.15) from 2.80 marks ($1.62).
Sales jumped 43.1 percent to 1.713 billion marks ($991.9 million).

However, Adidas said its marketing and administrative costs had jumped 48 percent to 481 million marks ($278.5 million), largely due to promotion costs related to a new brand of training shoes and the upcoming soccer world championship.
During the first quarter, traditionally one of the group's strongest, Adidas saw a 32 percent jump in sport shoe sales to 785 million marks ($454.5 million).
The group's new shoe line called "Feet You Wear," launched in the 1996 third quarter, continued to fare well, it said.
Sportswear sales jumped 56 percent, led by women's and children's wear.
Sales in the Asia/Pacific region, the group's fastest growing market, more than doubled to 183 million marks ($106.0 million), Adidas said.
Sales in North America jumped by 75 percent to 395 million marks ($228.7 million), largely buoyed by strong sales of the "Running" shoe brand and sportwear.
In Europe, still Adidas' largest market, the group's first-quarter sales rose by 29 percent to 1.1 billion marks ($636.9 million).
